7.stem: The student wants to explain to a general audience why volcanic soils tend to be fertile. Which choice best accomplishes this goal?

options.A: Crops need minerals such as potassium, phosphorus, and magnesium, and regions with volcanic soils, such as parts of Java, support unusually dense farming populations.
options.B: Although volcanic eruptions can destroy nearby farmland in the short term, regions with volcanic soils, such as parts of Java, support unusually dense farming populations.
options.C: Java, which is one of the most densely populated islands on Earth, has long supported dense farming populations, and much of its farmland lies on volcanic soils.
options.D: As volcanic ash weathers, it releases minerals such as potassium and phosphorus that crops need as nutrients, which is why volcanic soils tend to be fertile.

8.stem: The student wants to emphasize the study's main finding. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.B: Rourke found that peak algal-bloom coverage in the aerated pond dropped from 60 percent of the surface to 22 percent, while coverage in an untreated pond nearby rose from 39 percent to 55 percent.
options.C: Rourke found that peak algal-bloom coverage in the aerated pond dropped from 52 percent of the surface to 9 percent, while coverage in an untreated pond nearby rose from 41 percent to 47 percent.
options.D: Rourke found that peak algal-bloom coverage in the aerated pond dropped from 45 percent of the surface to 12 percent, while coverage in an untreated pond nearby held steady near 40 percent.

10.stem: The student wants to explain why the finding surprised researchers. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.A: Varadi expected the exposed headland to retreat about 18 centimeters a year, yet it lost only 13 while the sheltered cove lost 28, a reversal she traces to foot traffic diverted by a boardwalk closure.
options.B: Varadi expected the exposed headland to retreat about 12 centimeters a year, yet it lost only 8 while the sheltered cove lost 18, a reversal she traces to burrowing by a colony of sand martins.
options.C: Varadi expected the exposed headland to retreat about 16 centimeters a year, yet it lost only 11 while the sheltered cove lost 24, a reversal she traces to winter frost heave in the cove's clay soils.
options.D: Varadi expected the exposed headland to retreat about 14 centimeters a year, yet it lost only 9 while the sheltered cove lost 21, a reversal she traces to runoff from a resurfaced car park.

11.stem: The student wants to present a cautious summary of the findings. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.C: Over the 10-week trial, evening use of the path rose by 23 percent, though Brathwaite cautions that the trial ran entirely in autumn, when daylight hours were shrinking week by week, so the increase cannot yet be credited to the lighting.
options.D: Over the 8-week trial, evening use of the path rose by 19 percent, though Brathwaite cautions that the counts came from a single sensor that could not separate walkers from cyclists, so the increase cannot yet be credited to the lighting.

17.stem: The student wants to acknowledge a limitation of the study. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.A: Anand's result is limited in scope, however: because every plot grew the single cultivar 'Concept' and irrigation volume was held at one fixed level, the 50 percent optimum may not hold for other cultivars or at other irrigation rates.
options.B: Anand's result is limited in scope, however: because every plot grew the single cultivar 'Salinas' and daytime air temperature was held at one fixed level, the 50 percent optimum may not hold for other cultivars or at other temperatures.
options.C: Anand's result is limited in scope, however: because every plot grew the single cultivar 'Nevada' and relative humidity was held at one fixed level, the 50 percent optimum may not hold for other cultivars or at other humidity levels.

19.stem: The writer wants to convey the sequence of milestones by which photography became faster and more widely accessible. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: From the eight-hour exposures of 1826 through the daguerreotype, Kodak's roll film, and eventually digital and phone cameras, photography grew steadily faster and more accessible.
options.B: The first permanent photograph — made in 1826 — required an eight-hour exposure.
options.C: The first digital camera prototype was constructed in 1975.
options.D: In 1888, Kodak's roll-film camera first made photography accessible to amateurs.

20.stem: The student wants to underscore how much the pace of the glacier's retreat has accelerated. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: The glacier's ice has thinned by 120 meters since 1980, a loss measured over the same forty years in which the terminus pulled back 2.5 km.
options.B: Retreat is measured by comparing aerial photographs of the terminus taken years apart, the method used for the 1900 to 1980 period as well.
options.C: The glacier pulled back 2.5 km in the 40 years after 1980, more than six times the 0.4 km it had lost over the previous eighty.
options.D: The glacier feeds a river that 2 million people rely on — and its terminus has been pulling back from that river's headwaters since 1900.

21.stem: The student wants to generalize the pattern in a way a skeptical reader would accept. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: Sulfide-using bacteria appeared at 11 of the 12 vents sampled, and across three different oceans, indicating they are a widespread foundation of vent ecosystems.
options.B: Researchers sampled the microbial mats growing at twelve separate hydrothermal vents in the course of the study.
options.C: These chemosynthetic bacteria form the base of the food web at the vents, supporting the tube worms and the other animals that crowd around the openings in the sea floor.
options.D: The one vent that lacked these bacteria turned out to have unusually low sulfide, the very compound on which the bacteria depend for the energy they supply to the food web.

23.stem: The student wants to explain why the study cannot prove that fiber actually causes lower heart disease risk. Which choice most effectively accomplishes this goal?

options.A: The study was substantial, following 5,000 participants across a full decade of annual dietary questionnaires.
options.B: Researchers found that participants who ate the most dietary fiber had the lowest risk of heart disease.
options.C: Because the study was observational rather than a controlled experiment, it can show only an association, not that fiber caused the lower risk.
options.D: Participants described their own diets on annual questionnaires across the ten years, and self-reported diet data is well known to be prone to recall errors.
